Listeners.//: One listener per credential class, both plain HTTP. Printers get their own port and reach /p/* only; everything else is served on UserPort. Neither carries a certificate - nginx terminates TLS in front of both, with a different one for each audience. Naming these makes Kestrel ignore ASPNETCORE_URLS.

Certificates.//: The printer-facing certificate authority. Its private key is the most sensitive secret here - custom_cert is exclusive, so this CA is each provisioned printer's entire trust store.
Certificates.//ContainerNetworks: Ranges that exist only inside this deployment - a container network. Addresses in them are never offered as somewhere a printer could reach. Docker's default is the default here; compose.yaml overrides it with the network it pins. A deployment whose real LAN uses 172.16/12 should empty this list.

XForwarded.//: Which proxy may speak for the client. Empty means the forwarded-headers middleware is not registered at all - see XForwardedOptions. Set KnownNetworks to the proxy's network; compose.yaml does this for the shipped stack.

PrusaConnect.//PrinterTls: One switch for both ends: the tls line written into a printer's ini, and whether a leaf is minted for nginx to present. It does not decide what this process binds - the printer listener is plain HTTP either way, because the record size the firmware needs is not something SslStream can emit. false is for reading the wire or running a rig - every printer token then crosses the network in clear, and startup warns about it.
PrusaConnect.//PrinterPort: What a printer connects to from outside, written into every provisioning snippet. 15443 rather than firmware's 443 default, which belongs to the people-facing proxy.
